decisions.claim: The migration instructions tell the user to put the setup link in argv, which the CLI no longer reads and which /proc exposes
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED, and it undid round 13's F2 fix completely: the code stopped reading argv but describeStatus() still printed `--enrol "<the whole link>"`. Anyone following the instructions would have published the link to every agent AND then sat at a prompt wondering why nothing happened. Instructions now say to paste when asked, and say why. A test asserts the text never shows a link after --enrol.

decisions.claim: The mgmt socket's 10s inactivity timeout can destroy the connection mid-enrolment, after the token was committed and the link burned
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. Fixed at the root rather than by raising the timeout: enrolment no longer commits a placeholder token at all. A new `whose_link` action returns the agent NAME without redeeming anything (the GET endpoint does not burn - the server says so), so the client looks up the agent's existing token BEFORE enrolling and sends the final value first time. The register-then-swap dance and its window are gone, set_socket_token deleted, and the connection also gets a 60s absolute deadline plus a reply() that is safe on a destroyed socket.

decisions.claim: --finish cannot clear the old unit on a rerun once the store is gone
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED - cleanup() returned early on alreadyDone, so a first run that shredded the store but could not reach the user bus left a disabled-but-present unit file that nothing could ever remove, waiting to start a second daemon at the next boot. The alreadyDone path now still attempts the stop and the file removal.

decisions.claim: A failed burn is suppressed while the daemon reports success
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED. burn() swallowed the failure and the reply said ok, so a link that stayed live for its remaining 15 minutes - replayable to re-point the agent at another token - was invisible. burn() now returns a boolean, the reply carries link_burned, and the CLI prints a warning naming the consequence.

decisions.claim: The world-connectable mgmt socket has no absolute deadline and can be held indefinitely
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED, and the same defect I fixed on the per-agent sockets in round 12 and did not carry across to this one. setTimeout is an inactivity timer, so a byte every nine seconds held a connection for days without ever producing a newline; enough of them exhaust file descriptors and no agent can connect. 60s absolute deadline added - generous because enrolment legitimately waits on two network round trips.

decisions.claim: The content-type test does not distinguish JSON from non-JSON
decisions.reason: CONFIRMED both ways: `includes('json')` accepted `text/notjson` and rejected `Application/JSON`, which is valid and merely differently cased. Now parses the media type properly - parameters dropped, lowercased, exact match or the structured +json suffix.

decisions.claim: Outbound setup fetches have neither a timeout nor a size limit
decisions.reason: Blind spot, and worth acting on: this runs inside the process holding every agent's credentials. AbortSignal.timeout(15s) plus a 256KB response ceiling checked against content-length and again after reading.

decisions.claim: The link is out of argv but still in the enrolment client's memory, under the same uid as the agents
decisions.reason: True and irreducible at this layer: the owner has to paste the link into SOME process running as them. What the fix bought is real - argv is world-readable to every process continuously, process memory needs ptrace of a short-lived process at the right moment. Worth stating in the docs rather than pretending it is closed.

decisions.claim: Profile-store writes are not fsynced before rename
decisions.reason: Real durability gap - a crash between rename and writeback can leave a truncated store. Out of scope for this phase, which is about who can read the file, not whether it survives power loss. Noted for the owner.

decisions.claim: Concurrent enrolments for the same link are not serialised
decisions.reason: Real but now much narrower: the server enforces single-use, and the local window is one round trip. The remaining case needs a burn failure AND a concurrent caller, and F4 now surfaces the burn failure. Not worth a lock in this phase.
